identity.name: KALYANI FORGE LIMITED
identity.industry: Auto Components — Forgings (engine / driveline / axle for PV, CV, off-road & agri; fuel-agnostic / EV-ready)

summary.oneLiner: Kalyani Forge is a deliberate margin-and-mix turnaround: by phasing out ~INR 40 cr of low-margin "non-fit" legacy/export business and concentrating on high-volume OEM/Tier-1 engine-driveline-axle programs, it held revenue flat (~INR 238 cr FY26) yet lifted FY26 EBITDA margin to 13.3% (from 11.1%) with a second straight ~15% quarter, delivering 14-year-high PAT of INR 9.32 cr. The next leg is operating-leverage-driven: management has set 15% EBITDA as a new floor and is guiding toward 20% within ~a year, while ramping new PV wheel-hub/EV-axle wins (SKF, Schaeffler) from Q1 FY27 — the swing factors are working-capital/cash-conversion normalization and capex execution.

one-line thesis: Kalyani Forge is a deliberate margin-and-mix turnaround: by phasing out ~INR 40 cr of low-margin "non-fit" legacy/export business and concentrating on high-volume OEM/Tier-1 engine-driveline-axle programs, it held revenue flat (~INR 238 cr FY26) yet lifted FY26 EBITDA margin to 13.3% (from 11.1%) with a second straight ~15% quarter, delivering 14-year-high PAT of INR 9.32 cr. The next leg is operating-leverage-driven: management has set 15% EBITDA as a new floor and is guiding toward 20% within ~a year, while ramping new PV wheel-hub/EV-axle wins (SKF, Schaeffler) from Q1 FY27 — the swing factors are working-capital/cash-conversion normalization and capex execution.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q4/FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Q4 ~INR 59.24 cr (gross); FY26 ~INR 238 cr | Flat YoY | Flat *despite* phasing out ~INR 40 cr non-fit business → core grew |
| EBITDA / margin | Q4 ~INR 9 cr (15.2%); FY26 INR 31.58 cr (13.3%) | FY25 EBITDA ~INR 26 cr (11.1%) | 2nd consecutive ~15% quarter = "new floor" |
| PBT | Q4 INR 6.13 cr; FY26 INR 14.37 cr | up | Driven mostly by higher EBITDA |
| PAT (rptd) | Q4 INR 5.88 cr; FY26 INR 9.32 cr | FY25 PAT ~INR 8.31 cr | FY26 = highest in ~14 years |
| EPS | Q4 INR 16.17; FY26 INR 25.6 | up | — |
| ROCE | 18% (Q4) | from 14% (Q1 FY26) | Improving capital efficiency |
| Debt / equity | 1.11 | up | Rose on growth capex + WC; target band 1.0–1.2 |
| Cash conversion cycle | improving sequentially | peaked 176 days (Q2) | Target step-1: 120–130 days |
| PPE / CWIP | PPE INR 86.5 cr (vs 60.5 cr LY); CWIP INR 10.3 cr | up | Incl. ~INR 10 cr dies/tooling reclassified from inventory |
> One-offs / distortions: (1) Q3 PAT was ~zero on a deferred-tax hit; Q4 PAT benefited from the reverse deferred-tax effect — mgmt says read Q3+Q4 PAT together, focus on EBITDA. (2) Q4 finance cost unusually low (~INR 0.24 cr vs ~INR 2 cr/qtr run-rate) because term-loan interest was capitalized with Q4 asset capitalization — use full-year interest. (3) Other income ~INR 2 cr higher YoY = export/govt incentives (recurring) + sale of obsolete fixed assets (routine). (4) ~INR 10 cr dies/tooling reclassified inventory→fixed assets (separate from the INR 23.44 cr cash capex).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Margin:** 15% EBITDA is now a "floor/baseline"; targeting **20% EBITDA within ~a year** (by end FY27 / early FY28). FY27 focus = sustain 15%+ and climb.
- **Revenue / capacity:** steady-state ~INR 300 cr turnover achievable at ~INR 90–99 cr fixed assets (using a ~3x fixed-asset-turn vs industry 1.5–2). New OEM wheel-hub orders (SKF, Schaeffler) ramp from Q1 FY27; EV high-volume axle order ~INR 20 cr annual revenue.
- **Working capital:** cash-conversion-cycle target step-1 120–130 days (from peak 176); ROCE improvement; WC reduction a key FY27 KPI.
- **Capex:** FY27 capex plan ~INR 30 cr (FY26 cash capex INR 23.44 cr). FY27 split by stage: existing ~INR 5 cr, ramp-up ~INR 10 cr, new ~INR 10 cr, future ~INR 5 cr; 60% to future-growth areas (driveline/axle). 
- **Capital structure:** maintain D/E 1.0–1.2; actively preparing for an **equity raise** ("legwork" / investor meetings underway — watch for dilution).
order book & pipeline:
- 3 major order wins in Q4: OEM wheel-hub programs for SKF and Schaeffler (bearings/PV), ramping from Q1 FY27.
- New EV high-volume **axle** order ~INR 20 cr annual revenue; additional business allocation from top customers in core engine (share-of-wallet gains).
- "New business order book" (slide 12) unchanged QoQ — flat because items converted to production (balance figure of what's yet to move to production), not a lack of wins.
- Programs are multi-year: typical 5–10 yr life cycle, many >10 yr, some up to 20 yr (if OEM design unchanged).
- OEM revenue reached INR 37.3 cr in FY26 (highest in ~2 years, upward trend).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Engine (~60% rev):** core, connecting-rod-led; serves heavy CV, off-road and agri — "cash cow," long-term visibility.
- **Driveline (~20%):** fast-growing, PV-led; fuel-agnostic (works in any drivetrain incl. EV).
- **Axle (~10%):** fast-growing, fuel-agnostic; new wins = Gen-3 wheel hubs (PV wheels) + EV high-volume axle.
- Kalyani Forge positions itself as the **only forging company offering engine + driveline + axle to the same OEM**, via combined hot + warm forging built over decades — driving share-of-wallet.
- Exports fell to ~11% of Q4 (deliberately — legacy non-fit export programs pruned); new export programs growing; export/govt incentives recur in other income.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **EV-agnostic driveline + axle** = structural growth + future-proofing (the picks-and-shovels EV angle: content stays regardless of powertrain).
- **PV wheel-hub (Gen-3) franchise** with global bearings majors (SKF, Schaeffler) — large market, repeatable, "future-proof."
- **Margin self-help:** Vriddhi Council (10 refined cost/margin projects), new **Plant Engineering** vertical (layout/electrical/utility redesign — low-capex OEE/uptime gains), forging modernization / machine reconditioning.
- **Operating leverage to ~INR 300 cr** on current asset base before major new capex needed.
margins & cost dynamics:
- EBITDA margin drivers (mgmt-ranked): (1) exit from low-margin business (the "painful" Q2/Q3 FY26 pruning); (2) Vriddhi Council cost/margin projects; (3) new Plant Engineering (layouts/utilities → OEE, low capex); (4) material + power cost discipline (supplier negotiation, forging-yield gains, simplified electrical circuits); (5) operational stabilization (machine recon, die-run prioritization → uptime/utilization).
- OEM mix shift adds value → better pricing → structurally better margin.
- Target: 15% floor now, 20% within a year.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- FY26 cash capex INR 23.44 cr (excludes the ~INR 10 cr dies/tooling reclassification); FY27 plan ~INR 30 cr.
- FY27 capex is customer-program-aligned at granular level (Phase-4 "resource reallocation"); 60% to future-growth/high-ROC; bias to driveline/axle ramp + bottleneck removal / OEE uplift.
- Fixed-asset turn deliberately falling from a stretched 3.5–4x toward industry 1.5–2x as asset base modernizes (steady-state assumed ~3x).
capital allocation:
- Maintain D/E 1.0–1.2 (currently 1.11).
- Preparing for an equity raise (balance-sheet strengthening; positive early investor feedback) — potential dilution catalyst to watch.
- Reinvestment-led; no buyback/dividend emphasis on call. Inventory rationalized; dies/tooling reclassified to fixed assets per industry best practice.
risks & watch-items:
- **Working-capital stretch:** receivables growing faster than sales (credit terms + customer safety-stock/JIT warehousing commitments); CCC peaked 176 days — execution on the 120–130 day target is the key de-risking proof point.
- **Margin durability:** 20% target is ambitious vs a sub-scale ~INR 238 cr topline; depends on ramp of new OEM programs and sustained cost programs.
- **Revenue scale / customer concentration:** small base; heavy reliance on a few OEM/Tier-1 (SKF, Schaeffler) and growing share-of-wallet = concentration risk.
- **Equity dilution risk** from the planned raise.
- **Leverage:** D/E rose to 1.11 on growth + WC.
- **Accounting normalization in progress:** clean-audit roadmap (Phase 2, external consultant, SAP/ledger clean-up), capitalization-timing effects, deferred-tax swings distort optical quarterly PAT.
- **End-market cyclicality:** CV / off-road / agri (engine) and PV (driveline/axle) demand cycles.
management quality / tone: - MD Viraj Kalyani candid and granular; emphasized EBITDA over optical quarterly PAT, openly explained the deferred-tax and interest-capitalization distortions, and framed the "painful" low-margin exits honestly. Strong operational-improvement narrative (Vriddhi Council, Plant Engineering, machine recon) with credible, low-capex levers. Governance focus (clean-audit roadmap, inventory/tooling reclassification) is a positive. Slightly promotional on the 20% margin / INR 300 cr potential, but hedged with timelines. Sole-voice call (no CFO) and a short, lightly-attended Q&A (~3 questioners) are minor quality caveats.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The flat topline understates the turnaround: stripping ~INR 40 cr of deliberately-shed non-fit revenue means the *core* OEM business grew meaningfully while margins re-rated — a classic "shrink-to-grow" inflection.
- The real value driver is being the **only forger offering engine + driveline + axle to one OEM** (hot+warm forging) — that's the share-of-wallet moat behind the SKF/Schaeffler wins.
- Driveline + axle being **fuel-agnostic** means the EV transition is content-neutral-to-positive, not a threat — a defensive feature rare among ICE-exposed auto-component names.
- Margin upside is largely **self-help and low-capex** (Plant Engineering, layout/utility redesign, machine recon) rather than dependent on volume — so the 20% target is more controllable than typical for a small forger.
- Watch the equity raise: it caps balance-sheet risk but the dilution timing/price is the swing factor for per-share value.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

identity.name: KALYANI FORGE LIMITED
identity.industry: Auto Components — Forgings (engine / driveline / axle for PV, CV, off-road & agri; fuel-agnostic / EV-ready)

hero.oneLiner: Kalyani Forge is a deliberate margin-and-mix turnaround: by phasing out ~INR 40 cr of low-margin "non-fit" legacy/export business and concentrating on high-volume OEM/Tier-1 engine-driveline-axle programs, it held revenue flat (~INR 238 cr FY26) yet lifted FY26 EBITDA margin to 13.3% (from 11.1%) with a second straight ~15% quarter, delivering 14-year-high PAT of INR 9.32 cr. The next leg is operating-leverage-driven: management has set 15% EBITDA as a new floor and is guiding toward 20% within ~a year, while ramping new PV wheel-hub/EV-axle wins (SKF, Schaeffler) from Q1 FY27 — the swing factors are working-capital/cash-conversion normalization and capex execution.
hero.industry: Auto Components — Forgings (engine / driveline / axle for PV, CV, off-road & agri; fuel-agnostic / EV-ready)

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims unique breadth: "Kalyani Forge is the only forging company to offer Engine + Driveline + Axle components to OEMs, due to a combination of Hot and Warm forging technologies built over decades."
- Technology firsts cited in milestones: "1st Fracture Split Conrod developed in India", "Started Warm Forging (1st in India)", and "1st Euro-6/BS VI compliant conrod in India".
- Founding is stated two ways in the same deck: "Established in 1978, around 50 years in the industry" (Company Stats) and "Founded in 1979 by Dr. Neelkanth Kalyani (Founder of Kalyani Group)" (Milestones).
- End-market spread framed as a hedge: Trucks and Cars are "large and mature market" with "high volume and high value forgings in every truck / car", while Industrial and Agro are each described as a "hedge against cyclicality of automotive markets" leveraging "automotive standards expertise to differentiate with competitors".
- Deck flags a "Leadership transition to next generation" on the Board slide (Rohini Kalyani Executive Chairperson, Viraj Kalyani Managing Director).

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Engine (~60% rev):** core, connecting-rod-led; serves heavy CV, off-road and agri — "cash cow," long-term visibility.
- **Driveline (~20%):** fast-growing, PV-led; fuel-agnostic (works in any drivetrain incl. EV).
- **Axle (~10%):** fast-growing, fuel-agnostic; new wins = Gen-3 wheel hubs (PV wheels) + EV high-volume axle.
- Kalyani Forge positions itself as the **only forging company offering engine + driveline + axle to the same OEM**, via combined hot + warm forging built over decades — driving share-of-wallet.
- Exports fell to ~11% of Q4 (deliberately — legacy non-fit export programs pruned); new export programs growing; export/govt incentives recur in other income.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- 3 major order wins in Q4: OEM wheel-hub programs for SKF and Schaeffler (bearings/PV), ramping from Q1 FY27.
- New EV high-volume **axle** order ~INR 20 cr annual revenue; additional business allocation from top customers in core engine (share-of-wallet gains).
- "New business order book" (slide 12) unchanged QoQ — flat because items converted to production (balance figure of what's yet to move to production), not a lack of wins.
- Programs are multi-year: typical 5–10 yr life cycle, many >10 yr, some up to 20 yr (if OEM design unchanged).
- OEM revenue reached INR 37.3 cr in FY26 (highest in ~2 years, upward trend).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Margin:** 15% EBITDA is now a "floor/baseline"; targeting **20% EBITDA within ~a year** (by end FY27 / early FY28). FY27 focus = sustain 15%+ and climb.
- **Revenue / capacity:** steady-state ~INR 300 cr turnover achievable at ~INR 90–99 cr fixed assets (using a ~3x fixed-asset-turn vs industry 1.5–2). New OEM wheel-hub orders (SKF, Schaeffler) ramp from Q1 FY27; EV high-volume axle order ~INR 20 cr annual revenue.
- **Working capital:** cash-conversion-cycle target step-1 120–130 days (from peak 176); ROCE improvement; WC reduction a key FY27 KPI.
- **Capex:** FY27 capex plan ~INR 30 cr (FY26 cash capex INR 23.44 cr). FY27 split by stage: existing ~INR 5 cr, ramp-up ~INR 10 cr, new ~INR 10 cr, future ~INR 5 cr; 60% to future-growth areas (driveline/axle). 
- **Capital structure:** maintain D/E 1.0–1.2; actively preparing for an **equity raise** ("legwork" / investor meetings underway — watch for dilution).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **EV-agnostic driveline + axle** = structural growth + future-proofing (the picks-and-shovels EV angle: content stays regardless of powertrain).
- **PV wheel-hub (Gen-3) franchise** with global bearings majors (SKF, Schaeffler) — large market, repeatable, "future-proof."
- **Margin self-help:** Vriddhi Council (10 refined cost/margin projects), new **Plant Engineering** vertical (layout/electrical/utility redesign — low-capex OEE/uptime gains), forging modernization / machine reconditioning.
- **Operating leverage to ~INR 300 cr** on current asset base before major new capex needed.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- EBITDA margin drivers (mgmt-ranked): (1) exit from low-margin business (the "painful" Q2/Q3 FY26 pruning); (2) Vriddhi Council cost/margin projects; (3) new Plant Engineering (layouts/utilities → OEE, low capex); (4) material + power cost discipline (supplier negotiation, forging-yield gains, simplified electrical circuits); (5) operational stabilization (machine recon, die-run prioritization → uptime/utilization).
- OEM mix shift adds value → better pricing → structurally better margin.
- Target: 15% floor now, 20% within a year.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Maintain D/E 1.0–1.2 (currently 1.11).
- Preparing for an equity raise (balance-sheet strengthening; positive early investor feedback) — potential dilution catalyst to watch.
- Reinvestment-led; no buyback/dividend emphasis on call. Inventory rationalized; dies/tooling reclassified to fixed assets per industry best practice.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - MD Viraj Kalyani candid and granular; emphasized EBITDA over optical quarterly PAT, openly explained the deferred-tax and interest-capitalization distortions, and framed the "painful" low-margin exits honestly. Strong operational-improvement narrative (Vriddhi Council, Plant Engineering, machine recon) with credible, low-capex levers. Governance focus (clean-audit roadmap, inventory/tooling reclassification) is a positive. Slightly promotional on the 20% margin / INR 300 cr potential, but hedged with timelines. Sole-voice call (no CFO) and a short, lightly-attended Q&A (~3 questioners) are minor quality caveats.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Working-capital stretch:** receivables growing faster than sales (credit terms + customer safety-stock/JIT warehousing commitments); CCC peaked 176 days — execution on the 120–130 day target is the key de-risking proof point.
- **Margin durability:** 20% target is ambitious vs a sub-scale ~INR 238 cr topline; depends on ramp of new OEM programs and sustained cost programs.
- **Revenue scale / customer concentration:** small base; heavy reliance on a few OEM/Tier-1 (SKF, Schaeffler) and growing share-of-wallet = concentration risk.
- **Equity dilution risk** from the planned raise.
- **Leverage:** D/E rose to 1.11 on growth + WC.
- **Accounting normalization in progress:** clean-audit roadmap (Phase 2, external consultant, SAP/ledger clean-up), capitalization-timing effects, deferred-tax swings distort optical quarterly PAT.
- **End-market cyclicality:** CV / off-road / agri (engine) and PV (driveline/axle) demand cycles.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The flat topline understates the turnaround: stripping ~INR 40 cr of deliberately-shed non-fit revenue means the *core* OEM business grew meaningfully while margins re-rated — a classic "shrink-to-grow" inflection.
- The real value driver is being the **only forger offering engine + driveline + axle to one OEM** (hot+warm forging) — that's the share-of-wallet moat behind the SKF/Schaeffler wins.
- Driveline + axle being **fuel-agnostic** means the EV transition is content-neutral-to-positive, not a threat — a defensive feature rare among ICE-exposed auto-component names.
- Margin upside is largely **self-help and low-capex** (Plant Engineering, layout/utility redesign, machine recon) rather than dependent on volume — so the 20% target is more controllable than typical for a small forger.
- Watch the equity raise: it caps balance-sheet risk but the dilution timing/price is the swing factor for per-share value.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** FY26 PAT INR 9.32 cr (14-yr high), EPS INR 25.6; revenue flat ~INR 238 cr but ~INR 40 cr non-fit business shed → core grew; FY26 EBITDA INR 31.58 cr / 13.3% (vs 11.1% FY25), 2nd straight ~15% quarter (Q4 15.2%); Q4 PAT INR 5.88 cr (deferred-tax reversal vs ~zero Q3); ROCE 18% (Q4) from 14% (Q1); D/E 1.11; CCC improving from 176-day Q2 peak. New wins: SKF/Schaeffler PV wheel hubs + ~INR 20 cr/yr EV axle, ramping Q1 FY27. Capex INR 23.44 cr FY26, ~INR 30 cr FY27 plan. Equity raise in preparation.
- _Next Q → check: (1) EBITDA toward 20% target / 15% floor held? (2) CCC down to 120–130 days, receivables normalizing? (3) SKF/Schaeffler hub + EV axle ramp visible in revenue? (4) D/E within 1.0–1.2; (5) equity raise announced (size/price/dilution); (6) FY27 capex ~INR 30 cr on plan; (7) clean-audit roadmap Phase 2 progress._
